hot.title: PiD: Fast and High-Resolution Latent Decoding with Pixel Diffusion
hot.summary: PiD reformulates latent decoding as a conditional pixel diffusion process, unifying latent-to-pixel mapping and spatial upsampling into a single generative module. This approach generates high-resolution images (up to 4K) from various latent representations, achieving superior visual quality and significantly lower inference latency compared to prior methods.

hot.title: Vector Policy Optimization: Training for Diversity Improves Test-Time Search
hot.summary: Vector Policy Optimization (VPO) trains large language models to generate diverse candidate solutions by leveraging vector-valued reward structures and stochastic scalarization. This method consistently achieves higher best@k scores and maintains greater reward-space diversity compared to scalar reinforcement learning baselines across multiple domains, significantly enhancing performance in test-time search applications.

hot.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills
hot.summary: SkillOpt introduces a text-space optimization framework for refining natural-language agent skills, allowing frozen large language models to acquire and adapt procedural knowledge. The method achieves consistent performance gains across various benchmarks and models, improving average accuracy by up to +39.0 points on specific procedural tasks while generating compact and transferable skill artifacts.

hot.title: Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search
hot.summary: Google DeepMind, Aarhus University, and Google researchers developed AlphaProof Nexus, an AI-driven formal proof search framework that autonomously resolved several open, research-level problems in mathematics by integrating large language models with the Lean proof assistant. The system successfully generated mechanically verifiable proofs for long-standing conjectures in various mathematical domains, addressing the unreliability of natural language AI in complex mathematical reasoning.

hot.title: GenRecon: Bridging Generative Priors for Multi-View 3D Scene Reconstruction
hot.summary: Researchers from Technical University of Munich and Huawei Technologies developed GenRecon, a method that adapts an object-level generative model to reconstruct high-fidelity, complete, and relightable PBR meshes of entire 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images. It achieved superior geometric accuracy and completeness on ScanNet++ and 3D-FRONT datasets compared to existing reconstruction techniques.

hot.title: Training-Free Looped Transformers
hot.summary: Researchers at the University of Texas at Austin introduced a training-free method to enhance large language model performance at inference time by augmenting frozen transformer checkpoints with a recurrent structure. This approach, which interprets transformer blocks as ODE integration steps, iteratively refines internal representations, achieving performance gains of up to +2.64 percentage points on knowledge-intensive benchmarks with controlled computational overhead.

hot.title: Gated DeltaNet-2: Decoupling Erase and Write in Linear Attention
hot.summary: Gated DeltaNet-2, developed by researchers at NVIDIA, enhances linear recurrent attention models by decoupling memory erase and write operations through distinct channel-wise gates. This refined approach improves performance across language modeling, common-sense reasoning, and retrieval tasks, showing particular gains on long-context benchmarks requiring robust interference control.

hot.title: LLMs as Noisy Channels: A Shannon Perspective on Model Capacity and Scaling Laws
hot.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, University of Virginia, and University of California, Berkeley introduced the Shannon Scaling Law, a theoretical framework that models Large Language Model (LLM) training as information transmission over a noisy channel to explain both monotonic and non-monotonic scaling behaviors. The framework demonstrated superior fitting accuracy (R² up to 0.9824) and extrapolation capabilities compared to existing scaling laws across various perturbation scenarios like Gaussian noise, supervised fine-tuning, and quantization, consistently predicting U-shaped loss curves.

hot.title: StepAudio 2.5 Technical Report
hot.summary: The StepFun-Audio Team introduces StepAudio 2.5, a unified audio-language foundation model that matches or exceeds the performance of specialized systems across Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR), Text-to-Speech (TTS), and realtime spoken interaction. This is achieved through extensive post-training optimization, including task-tailored Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback, and results in improved efficiency for ASR, higher preference scores for TTS, and superior conversational quality for realtime applications.

hot.title: WorldKV: Efficient World Memory with World Retrieval and Compression
hot.summary: WorldKV presents a training-free framework for autoregressive video world models, allowing them to sustain persistent and consistent explorable worlds over long durations while maintaining real-time inference speeds. It achieves this by selectively retrieving and compressing Key-Value (KV) cache chunks, matching or exceeding the memory fidelity of full KV-cache attention while doubling throughput.

hot.title: Geo-Align: Video Generation Alignment via Metric Geometry Reward
hot.summary: Researchers from USTC and Shanghai AI Lab developed Geo-Align, a reinforcement learning framework for camera-controlled video generation that uses a metric geometry reward to synthesize novel-view videos precisely following target camera trajectories. The system improves geometric consistency, camera accuracy, and visual quality, outperforming supervised learning baselines on real-world datasets.

hot.title: Self-Policy Distillation via Capability-Selective Subspace Projection
hot.summary: The Self-Policy Distillation (SPD) framework enables large language models to improve through self-distillation without external signals, utilizing a novel method to extract and project intermediate representations onto a capability-specific subspace. This approach consistently yields up to 13% relative improvement over prior self-distillation techniques, demonstrating strong in-domain and out-of-domain generalization across tasks like code generation, mathematical reasoning, and question answering.

hot.title: Any2Any: Efficient Cross-Embodiment Transfer for Humanoid Whole-Body Tracking
hot.summary: LimX Dynamics researchers developed ANY2ANY, a framework for efficiently transferring pre-trained humanoid Whole-Body Tracking (WBT) policies across different robot embodiments. The method, which combines kinematic alignment with low-rank adaptation (LoRA), enables adaptation with only approximately 1% of the compute and data required for training from scratch, while achieving comparable or superior tracking performance.

hot.title: HorizonStream: Long-Horizon Attention for Streaming 3D Reconstruction
hot.summary: HorizonStream provides a Transformer architecture for streaming 3D reconstruction that maintains stable and accurate camera pose estimation and dense scene reconstruction over ultra-long video sequences. It introduces a novel attention mechanism with learned channel-wise retention rates, enabling adaptive, multi-timescale management of geometric evidence.

hot.title: Cambrian-P: Pose-Grounded Video Understanding
hot.summary: A model named Cambrian-P augments multimodal large language models for video understanding with explicit camera pose grounding, addressing limitations in spatial reasoning. This approach achieves a 4.5% accuracy improvement on VSI-Bench and records a minimal Absolute Trajectory Error of 0.078 on ScanNet for streaming pose estimation.

hot.title: Code as Agent Harness
hot.summary: Researchers from the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Meta, and Stanford University present a conceptual framework, "code as agent harness," repositioning code from an LLM output to an operational substrate enabling robust agent intelligence. This work systematizes how code facilitates agent reasoning, action, environment modeling, and verifiable long-horizon task execution through a three-layered taxonomy.

hot.title: Generative Recursive Reasoning
hot.summary: Researchers from KAIST, Mila, New York University, and Université de Montréal introduced Generative Recursive Reasoning Models (GRAM), a framework that injects stochasticity into recursive neural networks to enable multi-hypothesis exploration and generative capabilities. GRAM achieves improved performance on complex structured reasoning and multi-solution constraint satisfaction problems, outperforming deterministic recursive baselines and demonstrating high-quality unconditional generation of diverse data.

hot.title: SCOPE: Simulating Cross-game Operations in Playable Environments for FPS World Models
hot.summary: Researchers introduce SCOPE, an interactive world model for FPS games that employs a spatially selective action conditioning module within a video diffusion transformer to accurately simulate high-frequency control signals. The model achieves superior action responsiveness and spatial stability, demonstrating zero-shot generalization across diverse, unseen FPS environments, and is supported by the new CrossFPS multi-game dataset.

hot.title: Point Tracking Improves World Action Models
hot.summary: This research introduces JOPAT, a unified world-action model that jointly denoises visual latents, 2D point tracks with visibility, and robot actions within a diffusion transformer to improve robotic manipulation. JOPAT achieved a 97.8% average success rate on the LIBERO benchmark and an average of 57.5% on real-world LeRobot tasks, outperforming pixel-based baselines and demonstrating enhanced robustness to partial observability and distribution shifts.

hot.title: Strong Teacher Not Needed? On Distillation in LLM Pretraining
hot.summary: Researchers from Princeton University systematically re-examined the fundamental assumptions of knowledge distillation in Large Language Model pretraining, demonstrating that weaker teachers can provide benefits (e.g., 1.3% downstream accuracy improvement for a 0.7B teacher to a 1.7B student) and that excessively strong or overtrained teachers can sometimes degrade student performance.

likes.title: Perception Encoder: The best visual embeddings are not at the output of  the network
likes.summary: Perception Encoder introduces a family of vision models that achieve state-of-the-art performance across diverse vision and vision-language tasks, demonstrating that general, high-quality visual features can be extracted from the intermediate layers of a single, contrastively-trained network. It provides specific alignment tuning methods to make these features accessible for tasks ranging from zero-shot classification to dense spatial prediction and multimodal language understanding.

likes.title: TTRL: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: TTRL is a framework enabling Large Language Models to self-improve through Reinforcement Learning on unlabeled test data, using self-generated rewards derived from majority voting. This approach substantially boosts performance on complex reasoning tasks, with one model achieving a 211% improvement on AIME 2024, by fostering a self-reinforcing learning loop.

likes.title: Inference-Time Scaling for Generalist Reward Modeling
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI and Tsinghua University developed Self-Principled Critique Tuning (SPCT) and DeepSeek-GRM models, a pointwise generative reward modeling approach that achieves state-of-the-art performance in generalist reward benchmarks. This method demonstrates effective inference-time scalability, allowing smaller models to match or exceed the performance of much larger models by leveraging increased compute during inference, thereby improving LLM alignment.

likes.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?
likes.summary: Research from Tsinghua University reveals that current Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) primarily enhances the sampling efficiency of Large Language Models for already existing reasoning patterns. This optimization often narrows the models' overall reasoning capacity at higher pass@k values, contrasting with distillation, which effectively expands their problem-solving scope.

likes.title: Reasoning Models Can Be Effective Without Thinking
likes.summary: Ma et al. demonstrated that Large Language Models trained for Chain-of-Thought reasoning can achieve comparable or superior performance without generating explicit reasoning steps, utilizing a technique called 'NoThinking'. This approach significantly reduces inference latency by up to 9x and token usage by up to 5.1x, particularly when combined with parallel sampling, offering a more efficient paradigm for LLM reasoning.

likes.title: Synthetic Data Generation & Multi-Step RL for Reasoning & Tool Use
likes.summary: SWiRL is an offline multi-step reinforcement learning methodology designed to enhance Large Language Models' reasoning and tool-use capabilities. It generates and utilizes synthetic data, applying process-based filtering for step-wise optimization, which leads to substantial performance gains and strong cross-domain generalization in complex tasks.

likes.title: ReTool: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Tool Use in LLMs
likes.summary: ReTool, developed by ByteDance Seed, introduces a reinforcement learning framework that enables Large Language Models to strategically use code interpreters for complex problem-solving. It achieved 67.0% accuracy on the AIME 2024 benchmark, significantly improving performance over text-based reasoning and demonstrating emergent self-correction capabilities in code generation.

likes.title: Hogwild! Inference: Parallel LLM Generation via Concurrent Attention
likes.summary: Researchers from Yandex, HSE University, and IST Austria developed "Hogwild! Inference," a protocol enabling multiple Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate text concurrently by sharing a dynamically updated attention Key-Value (KV) cache. This mechanism allows LLMs to self-organize and collaborate in real-time, achieving up to 3.6x speedup and improved accuracy on complex reasoning tasks.

likes.title: Challenges and Paths Towards AI for Software Engineering
likes.summary: This paper presents a strategic roadmap for the field of AI in software engineering, providing a comprehensive taxonomy of software development tasks and identifying nine key bottlenecks that impede current AI capabilities. It proposes a targeted set of research directions focused on data collection, training, and inference-time approaches to advance automated software development.

likes.title: DAPO: An Open-Source LLM Reinforcement Learning System at Scale
likes.summary: Researchers from ByteDance Seed, Tsinghua University, and The University of Hong Kong developed DAPO, an open-source reinforcement learning system for large language models. The system achieved 50 points on the AIME 2024 dataset with a Qwen2.5-32B model, surpassing the prior 47-point score of DeepSeek-R1-Zero-Qwen-32B while requiring 50% fewer training steps.

likes.title: Proof or Bluff? Evaluating LLMs on 2025 USA Math Olympiad
likes.summary: Researchers from ETH Zurich and INSAIT conducted the first evaluation of large language models on generating rigorous natural language proofs for problems from the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. The study found that most state-of-the-art models scored below 5% of the maximum points, with the highest-performing model, GEMINI-2.5-PRO, achieving only 24.4%, demonstrating fundamental shortcomings in advanced mathematical reasoning capabilities.

likes.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: DeepSeek-AI developed DeepSeek-R1, an LLM demonstrating that sophisticated reasoning capabilities can emerge through pure outcome-based reinforcement learning without reliance on human-annotated reasoning trajectories. The model achieved an AIME 2024 pass@1 accuracy of 77.9% with R1-Zero, and the multi-stage DeepSeek-R1 surpassed state-of-the-art models on numerous math, coding, and STEM benchmarks while exhibiting emergent self-reflection and dynamic strategy adaptation.

likes.title: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
likes.summary: The ReSearch framework enables Large Language Models to integrate multi-step reasoning with external search, learning interactively via reinforcement learning without supervised intermediate steps. It yields substantial performance gains on complex multi-hop question answering benchmarks and reveals emergent self-correction capabilities.

likes.title: Insights into DeepSeek-V3: Scaling Challenges and Reflections on Hardware for AI Architectures
likes.summary: DeepSeek-V3 showcases how a hardware-software co-design strategy can achieve state-of-the-art large language model performance using a comparatively modest cluster of 2,048 NVIDIA H800 GPUs. The paper highlights innovations like Multi-head Latent Attention, DeepSeekMoE, FP8 mixed-precision training, and a Multi-Plane Fat-Tree network, which collectively reduce memory consumption, lower training costs, and accelerate inference.

likes.title: One-Minute Video Generation with Test-Time Training
likes.summary: Researchers from NVIDIA and leading universities introduce Test-Time Training (TTT) layers within pre-trained Diffusion Transformers to generate one-minute-long videos from text storyboards, enabling coherent multi-scene narratives while addressing the computational limitations of traditional self-attention mechanisms for long sequences.

likes.title: Sequential Task Assignment and Resource Allocation in V2X-Enabled Mobile Edge Computing
How new data permeates LLM knowledge and how to dilute it
likes.summary: Research from Google DeepMind reveals how new knowledge permeates through large language models, demonstrating that surprising information (measured by token probability) leads to broader changes across model behavior, while introducing "stepping-stone" text augmentation and "ignore-k" update pruning techniques that reduce undesirable priming effects by 50-95%.

likes.title: Titans: Learning to Memorize at Test Time
likes.summary: Titans introduces a new neural memory module that learns to memorize information at test time and effectively combines with attention mechanisms for better long-term sequence modeling

likes.title: PHYBench: Holistic Evaluation of Physical Perception and Reasoning in  Large Language Models
likes.summary: PHYBench, a new benchmark developed by the School of Physics at Peking University, rigorously evaluates large language models' physical perception and reasoning using 500 original, human-curated physics problems. Evaluations revealed a substantial performance gap between LLMs and human experts, with the best LLM achieving 36.9% accuracy compared to the human baseline of 61.9%.

likes.title: Process Reward Models That Think
likes.summary: This research introduces THINKPRM, a generative process reward model that enables large language models to provide verbalized, long Chain-of-Thought (CoT) verification for their reasoning steps. The model, developed by a collaboration including University of Michigan and LG AI Research, achieves high performance with orders of magnitude less step-level supervision than traditional discriminative models, while significantly improving reliability and generalizability.
